title: Countering Neural Audio Codec Distortions in Watermarking with Adaptive Restoration
abstract: Neural audio codecs offer high compression efficiency but introduce structured and non-linear distortions that severely degrade audio watermarks. To address this, we propose an adaptive codec-aware restoration framework that reconstructs codec-distorted spectrograms prior to extraction. Our method employs a ConvNeXt-based U-Net to recover fine-grained spectrogram patterns and introduces a lightweight classifier to dynamically select specialized restoration models for each codec. Experimental results across various neural codecs demonstrate that our model improves bitwise accuracy from near-random levels to over 98% for RVQ-based codecs. Furthermore, by analyzing the impact of quantizer configurations on watermark survivability, we show that our method can effectively improve watermark robustness in modern codec environments.
relevance_note: Restoration of codec-distorted spectrograms for audio watermark extraction; watermark robustness rather than synthesis or codec design, consistent with rejected Latent-Mark and self-VC watermark-attack precedents.
